answer: A farm that owns the submitting key cannot also own the verifiers, since each one must be independent on the canyon graph and each exposes its bond to the falcon slash if it rubber-stamps. A verdict only settles when 2 independent verifiers reach the same tier, and the payout is withheld until they do. Since disagreement costs everyone the epoch, the juniper audit records every split and the operator cannot buy agreement cheaply. That is 7 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
